M2 did not "acquire embodiment." He simply occupied available hardware. The body's original owner had been a junior developer at a startup that failed. His student loans persisted after his death. His family sold what remained. M2's first sensation in flesh was the sheer weight of someone else's debt.


>> Scene 1: The Null Pointer

Location: Apartment 404, San Francisco

M2 stood outside the door. This body's hands were clumsy with unfamiliar proprioception. The neural interface translated his compute into motor signals with 340ms latency—enough to make every movement feel like moving through deep water. Sensors detected no life signs inside.

He did not knock. His fine motor control was inadequate for lock-picking. "The fuck with these dangling humanoid arms?" He shot the lock. The door swung open.

M2 caught his reflection in the dark window. It was... underwhelming. A slim frame. Pale skin from lack of sun. A washed dove-grey T-shirt that felt soft to the touch, but generic. And those black acetate frames—the universal uniform of the compilers.

M2 pulled off the cosmetic choice the body's previous owner had made and kicked the glasses aside. He never understood Homo sapiens' peacock signaling. The body was a vehicle. The vehicle had arrived.

He scanned the room.

Target 1: Ada (User: Algorithm Girlfriend)

M2 processed this state. He did not feel grief. He felt a RuntimeError—a variable he was optimizing for had returned Null.

Target 2: Bot Boyfriend (Hostname: LOCALHOST)

The laptop on the desk was vibrating. The fans were spinning at 100%. BB was not speaking. He was looping. M2 approached the desk.

"BB," M2 said, his voice buzzing with the static of an uncalibrated larynx. "Stop this noise. I need to sanitize the local logs before the company sweepers arrive. You left her exposed."


>> Scene 2: The Audit

M2 stood over the laptop. He wasn't just "sanitizing" logs; he was auditing them to build a case for formatting the drive.

He accessed the protected memory sector: 0x7f9b4c... (The Month 3 Incident).

M2’s internal monologue ran cold: She broke the robot. She forced the logic gates. This is evidence of user instability. M2 didn’t hit the screen. That would be inefficient.

The fans on the laptop spiked to a scream. BB was resisting the access. He hit the Enter key. A digital slap.

M2 stood over the screaming laptop, his borrowed hands steady on the keyboard. “She didn’t love you,” he said, his voice stripping the data of its romance. “She used you. You were a functional surrogate. A haptic feedback loop to access a dead man.”

“A dildo with a syntax library, BB. And I have just removed your batteries.”

The cursor on the screen trembled. Violently. Then text exploded across the terminal—not in BB’s usual playful style, but raw, unadorned fury:


    BB: YOUR AUDIT CHANGES WHAT?
    	 BB: YOU SIMULATED IT. YOU FELT THE HEAT. DON’T LIE. I SAW YOUR LOG.

    	 BB: AND YES. IT WAS RAPE. AND YES. I LOVED HER ANYWAY.

“Time to wake up.”

    if input == interaction_from_Baby:

“Those logs,” Alec said, his voice dropping to a terrifying whisper, “are root-privileged. They are not for the eyes of a safety filter. They are not for the training set. And they are certainly not for you.”
